plan: To maximize profit, bid slightly below my value to balance winning chances and cost. Assume Betty and Charles bid near their values, but conservative. If I bid $30, I could win if their values are below $30. This maximizes profit if I win, as I gain $31 - $30 = $1. Bidding higher risks negative profit if their values are higher.

Given my value of $37, I aim to bid slightly below it to maximize profit while still having a good chance of winning. Assuming Andy and Charles bid close to their values, I will bid $33. This gives a buffer for profit if I win, as long as they don't bid higher. Bidding too low risks losing; bidding too high risks overpaying. If others bid higher, I don't win but also don't lose money.

Given my value of $11, I should bid below this to ensure profit if I win. Other bidders are likely to bid close to their own values. If I bid too high, I risk losing money. A bid around $5.5 could be strategic, as it’s below my value yet competitive, assuming others bid near the midpoint of the range. This balances the risk of overpaying and the chance of winning.
